payload.answer: For x ≠ 2, (x² − 4)/(x − 2) = x + 2. The original expression has domain ℝ \ {2}. The simplified expression x + 2 is defined at x = 2, whereas the original is not, so they are not equivalent at every real number; they agree exactly on ℝ \ {2}.

approaches.description: Factor the numerator and cancel the common nonzero factor only on the original domain.
approaches.reason: This directly establishes both the simplification and the excluded value.

proof_steps.justification: A quotient is defined only when its denominator is nonzero. Here x − 2 ≠ 0 exactly when x ≠ 2.
proof_steps.statement: The original expression is defined precisely for x ∈ ℝ \ {2}.

proof_steps.justification: On the original domain, x − 2 is nonzero, so ((x − 2)(x + 2))/(x − 2) = x + 2.
proof_steps.statement: For x ≠ 2, the expression simplifies to x + 2.

proof_steps.justification: At x = 2, x + 2 has value 4, but the original quotient has zero denominator and is undefined.
proof_steps.statement: The two expressions cannot be equivalent as expressions defined at every real number.
